questions.enonce_markdown:
Name and explain any FOUR importance of transport to commerce and industry.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Transport** is the movement of goods and people from one place to another. It is one of the main aids to trade, and commerce and industry depend on it. Its importance is as follows.

1. **It brings goods from producers to consumers.** Goods made or grown in one place (for example cocoa in the Centre Region) are carried to markets and towns far away. Without transport, trade would be limited to the area where the goods are produced.

2. **It supplies raw materials and machines to industry.** Factories receive raw materials, fuel and spare parts by road, rail or sea, and send their finished products to the market, so production can continue.

3. **It widens the market.** Good transport lets a business sell far from its base and even abroad, so sales and profits increase.

4. **It creates employment.** Drivers, loaders, mechanics, shippers and agents earn their living from transport, and so do the people who run the garages, ports and stations.

(Other correct points: it makes possible the specialisation of regions and countries, because each can send what it produces best; it creates place utility, since goods become valuable when they reach the place where they are wanted; it reduces price differences between places and shortages of goods; it develops towns, tourism and trade; it allows quick delivery of perishable goods.)

**Conclusion.** Efficient transport lowers the cost and delay of moving goods and therefore helps commerce and industry to grow.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Outline any FOUR reasons for using a bill of lading.

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** A **bill of lading** is a document issued by the shipping company (or its agent) to the exporter when goods are loaded on a ship. It is used for the following reasons.

1. **It is a receipt for the goods.** It proves that the shipping company has received the goods on board in the stated quantity and condition.
2. **It is evidence of the contract of carriage.** It shows the terms on which the shipping company agrees to carry the goods to the named port.
3. **It is a document of title.** The person who holds the original bill of lading (and has endorsed it) has the right to collect the goods at the port of destination; it can be transferred to another person to sell the goods during the voyage.
4. **It is used for customs clearance and insurance claims.** The importer must present it, with other documents, to clear the goods; it also supports a claim if the goods are lost or damaged.

(Other points: it is used by banks as proof of shipment in payments by letter of credit; it gives details of the goods, ship, ports and freight charged.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Explain how will the following protect consumers:

(i) Price Control.

(ii) Department of Veterinary.

(iii) Trade Description Act.

(8 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** **Consumer protection** means the measures taken by governments, associations and the law to safeguard buyers from unfair, unsafe or dishonest practices by sellers. The three bodies or measures named protect consumers in different ways.

**(i) Price control.** The government fixes a **maximum price** (price ceiling) for certain essential goods and services such as bread, fuel or transport fares. Sellers cannot charge more than this price. Consumers are therefore protected against **exploitation and sudden price increases**, mainly in times of scarcity. Inspectors may check shops and markets and punish sellers who break the rule. (A weakness is that sellers may hide the goods and create a black market.)

**(ii) Department of Veterinary (veterinary services).** This department looks after the **health of animals and the safety of animal products**. Its officers inspect livestock, slaughterhouses, markets and shops that sell meat, fish, milk and eggs, and they vaccinate animals and control animal diseases. They condemn and remove unfit meat from sale. Consumers are protected against **diseased or unhealthy food** and so their health is safeguarded.

**(iii) Trade Description Act.** A law that forbids sellers to give **false or misleading descriptions** of goods or services, in labels, advertisements, quantity, quality, origin, price or the ingredients. A seller who breaks it may be fined or taken to court. Consumers are protected against **cheating and false advertising**, and they can choose with correct information and claim compensation.

**Conclusion.** Price control protects the consumer's pocket, the veterinary department protects his health and the Trade Description law protects him against dishonest descriptions.
